quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Is it safe to ride on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because drivers will see you easily.
No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, because a passenger can tell the driver you are there.
No, because it is illegal. You must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This position is most visible in the driver's rearview mirror.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders together.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcyclists: the left side, center, and right side of the lane.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, how do they appear to other drivers?

options.text: Going faster than they actually are
Going slower than they actually are
Not moving when they actually are

questions.correctAnswerText: Going faster than they actually are
questions.explanation: Because of their small size, motorcycles may look like they are going faster than they really are.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you will slow down suddenly
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your signals do not work

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is not as noticeable as a car's two brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers see it, especially when you need to slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group
At the back of the group

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the lead rider
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, right behind the leader. This way, experienced riders behind them can watch and help if needed.

questions.question: Which type of sign can be rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black letters. These are regulatory signs that tell drivers what rules to follow on the road.

questions.question: Other drivers have trouble seeing motorcycles at night. What should a motorcycle rider do?

options.text: Sound their horn repeatedly at night
Stay directly in front of another vehicle to be seen in their headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed at night
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night: slow down, increase your following distance, use another vehicle's lights to see ahead, use your high beam headlight (unless near other vehicles), and change your lane position when needed.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Switch between high and low beam

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the high beam setting
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day. This helps other drivers see you better. Use high beam anytime you are not following or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before you hit it.
Slow down before you hit it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you hit it.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an obstacle, slow down as much as you can before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat. Roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front end just before hitting the object.

questions.question: To swerve, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to go. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast that hits you, where should you ride to have the most room to recover?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most room to recover if a wind blast from a passing vehicle affects your control.

questions.question: How do you do maximum straight-line braking?

options.text: Use the front brake, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: For maximum straight-line braking, apply the front and rear brakes at the same time. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the recommended settings for the extra weight.

questions.question: When making normal stops, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Alternate between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping. This should be your habit for all stops, even normal ones.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. Moving to the side near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Moving to the far side may cause the driver to merge back too soon. The center is the safest position.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular pre-ride inspections are important for safe riding.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you not move to the far side of the lane away from the passing driver?

options.text: It discourages the driver from cutting into your lane too early.
It encourages the driver to cut into your lane too early.
It encourages the driver to finish passing as quickly as possible.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the driver to cut into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane is dangerous. It may encourage the driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and seem slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their true location and speed.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This is safest. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to return too soon.

questions.question: If you must swerve, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip in the direction of your turn. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, how does it affect stopping distance?

options.text: Stopping distance is not a concern.
Stopping distance stays the same as a motorcycle without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping distance may increase.
questions.explanation: Adding weight to a motorcycle increases stopping distance. Start slowing down earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: When riding three-wheel motorcycles in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for a staggered formation. Groups of three-wheel motorcycles should ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action first, then the other.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving as separate actions. Do not brake while swerving because this may cause your motorcycle to tip over.
